simple.meaning: דִּכֵּן (dikkên) is a Hebrew word meaning “this.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דִּכֵּן (H1797) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:31, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דִּכֵּן (H1797) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דִּכֵּן (H1797) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דִּכֵּן (dikkên) / H1797 is traced through Daniel 2:31, Daniel 7:20, Daniel 7:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1797. dikken דִּכֵּן demonstrative pronoun common this, that ; only Daniel; Ezra uses דֵח ( דֵּח + demonstrative affix. n , W CG 111 ); — Dan 2:31 ד ׳צַלְמָא , 7:20-21 , ד ׳קַרְנָא .

occurrences.englishText: “You, O king, saw, and behold,* “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying.

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them,
